## Summary

The bug was in `app/Http/Controllers/ProfileController.ts:update()` — a correct `ProfileUpdateSchema` (name/email/password rules matching registration) already existed in `app/Http/Validators/ProfileValidator.ts` but was never wired up. The controller instead read the raw request body via `this.request.json()` with no validation, then persisted it with `User.forceUpdate()`, which bypasses both the mass-assignment `fillable` allowlist and the framework's protection on credential columns — letting a caller overwrite `id`, `passwordHash`, or any other column.

Fixed by switching the controller to `await this.validateBody(ProfileUpdateSchema)` (422s on a bad email, empty name, or short password, matching registration behavior) and persisting with the regular `User.update()` instead of `forceUpdate()`, so only the fillable `name`/`email`/`password` fields are ever written (`password` still gets hashed into `passwordHash` via the model's normal update path when present, and is skipped when blank, leaving the current password intact). Also fixed a wrong relative import path (`../../Validators/...` → `../Validators/...`) that the change surfaced.

Added `tests/ProfileController.test.ts` covering: rejection of a malformed email, rejection of an empty name, extra fields (`id`, `passwordHash`) being silently ignored while valid fields still save, a valid update lowercasing the email, rejection of a too-short password, and blank password preserving the existing hash — with unchanged-account assertions in every rejection case. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` (8 pass, 0 fail) both succeed, and `bunx guren check` reports no new issues.
